programme.title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
programme.sub-title: How Washington DC Came to Be
programme.desc: Uncovering the origins of the District of Columbia; how the location for the national government is chosen; the original design and vision for the city by artist and engineer Pierre Charles L'Enfant; the creation and history of the National Mall.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
programme.sub-title: The White House and the Presidency
programme.desc: Tracking the history and fortunes of the White House; visiting the White House, beginning with the Oval Office and Cabinet Room; visiting the parks adjoining the White House; the Jefferson and Franklin Delano Roosevelt memorials.

programme.title: England: From the Fall of Rome to the Norman Conquest
programme.sub-title: Exploring How England Came to Be
programme.desc: Seeing what makes Anglo-Saxon England so captivating; a brief survey of the traditional scholarship across the ages; Professor Paxton outlines how to form a picture of the Anglo-Saxons, including written evidence, literary sources and more.

programme.title: England: From the Fall of Rome to the Norman Conquest
programme.sub-title: The Rise and Fall of Roman Britain
programme.desc: England is forged in the crucible of the decline of the Romans; exploring the impact of the Romans on Britain, from Hadrian's Wall to the city of London; the role of Christianity, the state of language and the collapsing economy during this time.

programme.title: The Development of European Civilization
programme.sub-title: The Idea and Place of Europe
programme.desc: Beginning the understanding of Europe as not only a place but as an evolving laboratory of ideas; learning how these ideas continue to animate human life not only in Europe but throughout much of the world, no matter their nature.

programme.title: The Development of European Civilization
programme.desc: Understanding the medieval world through an introduction to feudalism; how the need for protection and justice becomes a paramount concern with the disappearance of Roman rule and the absence of a central authority's ability to impose law and order.

programme.title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
programme.desc: Some of the ways people think about the American West; how this vast, fascinating region comes into being; how it is shaped by centuries of myth-making; what about westward expansion fascinates every generation of Americans.

programme.title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
programme.sub-title: The West in the Colonial Era
